bull.b: The AP3 platform gives Acrivon a defined precision-oncology approach for discovering and developing targeted medicines. If validated clinically, response-signature matching could improve patient selection, differentiate candidates, and support a repeatable development model across the pipeline.

Very low leverage and positive equity provide greater financial flexibility than a similarly unprofitable company carrying substantial debt. This reduces interest and refinancing pressure, allowing more of the available capital to support clinical development and other operating priorities.

Routine director elections and auditor ratification indicate continuity in the company’s governance framework. Stable oversight can support consistent execution of the clinical strategy, preserve institutional knowledge, and reduce disruption while Acrivon advances its investigational pipeline.

bear.b: Acrivon remains entirely dependent on advancing investigational candidates because it has not yet established product revenue. Without commercial sales, operating scale and revenue visibility are limited, leaving future financial progress dependent on clinical development and eventual approval.

Large recurring net losses show that the current business model does not yet fund itself and will likely require continued external capital. Ongoing losses reduce the company’s ability to compound internally generated resources and increase dependence on successful pipeline execution.

Persistent negative free cash flow consumes resources before any product commercialization is established. Continued burn alongside declining assets can shorten financial runway and constrain clinical investment, making future financing needs an important structural risk to shareholders.
